# Cursor

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

A cursor with physics and intent: glides, dwells, presses, drags and leaves once the product acts. 9 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Cursor drags an object into place

`dv-cursor-drag` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · any

A grab-hand cursor drags a value cell (tilted about 15 deg, straightening as it drops), a folder into a grid, or a dashed selection marquee across a collage; the hand can squash +33 % on contact and relax.

- **Build:** cursorMove with the dragged object attached by a lagged spring (one per film) or a short delay. Anatomy: Object tilt -15 deg -> 0 on drop; drag expo-out; contact pop 3 f, relax 6 f. Sound: A drum on the drop.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Timing:** Drag 26-42 f; drop 8 f.
- **Use when:** Drag-and-drop features; selections.
- **Avoid when:** Dragged objects that do not tilt or lag (they look glued).

### Cursor glides in, dwells, then clicks

`dv-cursor-glide-dwell-click` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · any

The cursor enters (often rising from below), decelerates onto its target, rests 5-8 frames, then clicks; the button darkens for a few frames; the card or the camera can start pulling back or pushing in right after the press; or the cursor simply cuts on already over the button and presses.

- **Build:** cursorState({ moves, click }) + press() on the target. Anatomy: Travel 22-44 f on an ease-out (172 px in 22 f), dwell 10-16 f, press 6-12 f; macro variant: a hand pressing a cropped send button in close-up. Sound: A click on the press; a kick on the following cut.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Timing:** 40-70 f per click.
- **Use when:** Every click in a demo.
- **Avoid when:** Clicking on arrival with no dwell.

### The cursor leaves in flight once the product acts

`dv-cursor-exit-flight` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · any

After its click the cursor does not fade: it accelerates off the frame on a quad- or expo-in, banking upright as it goes (3 -> 270 px/f); or it travels to the next button, presses, and drifts off.

- **Build:** cursorMove with an exit move on E.buildIn off-frame. Anatomy: Exit speed x1.3-1.9 a frame; bank follows velocity. Sound: An impact as the last button is pressed. Materials: After the click the cursor does not just translate: it turns about 200 deg in 10 f (peak about 20 deg/f, expo-out) while it accelerates off the top-right like a flicked paper plane; no motion blur, so the turn reads as a run of poses.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Materials:** After the click the cursor does not just translate: it turns about 200 deg in 10 f (peak about 20 deg/f, expo-out) while it accelerates off the top-right like a flicked paper plane; no motion blur, so the turn reads as a run of poses.
- **Timing:** 14-22 f.
- **Use when:** After the last click of a demo moment.
- **Avoid when:** Fading the cursor; leaving it parked on screen.

### A pointer glyph turns to aim, then moves

`dv-pointer-glyph-aims` · product demo · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A small pointer shape (a paper plane, a triangle) first rotates to aim at its target, then travels; a tiny pointer drifts in an empty cell and the target appears exactly where it stops; a filled pointer glides into a vacated slot.

- **Build:** Cursor custom shape with cursorTilt then cursorMove. Anatomy: Rotate 30-90 deg over 16-20 f ease-out, then rise or glide; drift 2-4 px/f. Sound: None needed. Materials: Letter tiles in the pointer's path flip in 3D: a tile goes edge-on (a 4-6 px parallelogram) in about 4 f, starting 2-4 f before the pointer reaches it, a flipped tile shows its letter mirrored; the cut lands before the flip completes.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Materials:** Letter tiles in the pointer's path flip in 3D: a tile goes edge-on (a 4-6 px parallelogram) in about 4 f, starting 2-4 f before the pointer reaches it, a flipped tile shows its letter mirrored; the cut lands before the flip completes.
- **Timing:** 30-50 f.
- **Use when:** Illustrative, non-literal UI films.
- **Avoid when:** Pointers that move before they aim.

### Hover states fire along the cursor's path

`dv-hover-trail` · product demo · accent · energy calm · any

The cursor sweeps up in one expo-out and every row it passes gets a hover outline for a few frames; a hover on an icon brings a small tooltip; a cursor wanders between the input and cards while the UI eases back.

- **Build:** cursorState + per-element hover flags from the cursor's position at each frame. Anatomy: Hover 6-8 f per row; tooltip hold 28 f. Sound: A whoosh as it enters.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Timing:** Sweep 52 f (44 % in 10 %).
- **Use when:** Showing that a UI is alive and responsive.
- **Avoid when:** Hover states lasting longer than the pass.

### Several people at work at once

`pd-presence-cursors` · product demo · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

Two or three named cursors move and act on the same canvas at the same time, each in its own rhythm, while presence avatars stack in the corner, so collaboration reads without a word.

- **Build:** Draw each collaborator as src/fx/Cursor.tsx plus a name flag pinned 14 px right and 18 px below the tip (a 6 px-radius label with an initial and first name in C.white on C.ink, C.ink2 or C.mute), so identity comes from the label rather than from colour and the one accent stays free for the newest edit. Script each person as a list of {to, at, action} beats: travel on cursorArc (bow 0.15-0.25, its sign from rand(name)) on E.smooth at 6-14 px/f, with every start shifted by rand(name + i) × 10 f so no two cursors arrive or press on the same frame. Between beats each cursor wanders: every 24 f it eases on E.smooth to a new point within 6 px of its rest, picked with rand(name + floor(f / 24)), so no hand ever freezes. Each action lands on that person's press frame (pressAt): a note dropped onto the canvas on SPR.firm, a shape dragged with the item evaluated 2 f behind the cursor, or a label typed with TypeOn at 30 cps beside the flag; the newest edit takes a 2 px C.accent outline for 24 f, then relaxes to C.line. In the top bar, overlapping 28 px avatar circles with initials scale in on spr(f, join, SPR.micro) as each cursor first enters the frame.
- **Timing:** Shot 180-240 f; travel 6-14 px/f on E.smooth, arrivals and presses at least 6 f apart; wander ≤ 6 px per 24 f; one action every 30-50 f across all cursors; note settle on SPR.firm ≈ 16 f; accent outline 24 f; avatars on SPR.micro 6-10 f each; at most three cursors.
- **Use when:** Collaborative documents, whiteboards, design and planning tools: anything whose claim is 'together, live'.
- **Avoid when:** A single-user product, or a frame where the name flags would be too small to read; never more than three cursors, which turns into noise.

### The cursor as a character

`dv-cursor-as-character` · product demo · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

An oversized cursor (8-12 % of the frame height) with its own look lives in the shot: it banks into its motion within 2 frames, a thick 3D cursor half-spins about its axis and is edge-on at peak speed, a glossy cursor idles with slow decelerating drifts between clicks, an outlined cursor swings upright as it lands and morphs into an I-beam.

- **Build:** <Cursor shape scale shadow="cast"> with cursorTilt (swing) and a shape switch to ibeam. Anatomy: Size 120-170 px; bank = f(velocity); swing from -60 deg to upright over 3 f; idle drift 10 -> 0 px/f. Sound: Mouse clicks. Materials: A glossy 3D cursor (matte white body, a warm bevel gradient, soft drop shadow) rests on the first letter of a line, then rises and passes behind it for 6 f: the letter is drawn over the cursor's tip, as if the cursor were an object moving between layers of type.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Materials:** A glossy 3D cursor (matte white body, a warm bevel gradient, soft drop shadow) rests on the first letter of a line, then rises and passes behind it for 6 f: the letter is drawn over the cursor's tip, as if the cursor were an object moving between layers of type.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Travel 40-52 f (peak 50-80 px/f at about 50 %); swing 8 f.
- **Use when:** Launch films where the product is used by "you".
- **Avoid when:** Multiple cursor styles in one film.

### Cursor glyph follows context

`mi-cursor-glyph-context` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy any · walkthrough, feature, launch, vertical

The pointer changes shape with what it is over, as a real system pointer does: an I-beam over text, an open hand over something draggable, a closed fist while dragging, and the arrow everywhere else. Each change is a one-frame swap.

- **Build:** cursorState(f, { ..., shape: 'arrow', switches: [{ at, to: 'ibeam' }] }) and <Cursor shape={c.shape} />: the arrow keeps its tip at (x, y), the I-beam its visual centre, so a swap never moves the point that acts; the swap is a one-frame change on a whole frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor.Cursor`
- **Timing:** Swap in 1 f on the frame the hotspot crosses a rect edge; fist on the pressAt down stroke (4 f down, 8 f recoil); open hand for 6-10 f after the release; item trails the fist by 1-3 f; I-beam approaches at 15 px/f or less.
- **Use when:** A cursor drives a walkthrough that both types and drags, and the pointer must behave like the real system's rather than an arrow stamped on everything.
- **Avoid when:** The cursor only clicks buttons (the arrow is correct there), or a snappy vertical edit would flash the glyph changes past before they read.

### Guide cursor: arrive, hover, press

`mi-guide-cursor-hover-press` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy any · walkthrough, feature, launch, vertical

A cursor travels a bowed path to the element about to act, swings upright as it lands, presses with a short dip and a thin ring, and the target responds on the same frame.

- **Build:** const c = cursorState(f, { from, moves: [{ to, start, dur }], tilt: { from: -20, start }, click: { at, ring: true } }, film); <Cursor x={c.x} y={c.y} angle={c.angle} press={c.press} ring={c.ring} shadow='cast' />. The target's press (fx/Cards press) starts on the same frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor.cursorState`
- **Timing:** Move 44 f on E.glideOut, bow 0.18; tilt settles from 16-24 deg over 36 f on E.settleOut; ring 30 f, 10 -> 34 px.
- **Use when:** A person is driving the product, and dense UI needs a point of view that shows the viewer where to look next.
- **Avoid when:** The product acts on its own, clicks would come faster than one per 30 f, or the shot already has a pointer such as a focus ring.
